questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Out of bounds
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Forbidden.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Given Idiom: ***Out of bounds*** means forbidden; not allowed.

 
 
• *Example: The path by the railway line is officially **out of bounds** to both cyclists and walkers*.
 
 
 
• From the given options, the first option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

__
 
• We may think from the phrase "Out of bounds" that it means limitless, but the correct answer is option 1. So be careful while dealing with such questions.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• *This expression alludes to the boundaries of the playing area in numerous sports and to the rules applying to them. Its figurative use dates from the 1940s*.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Fire the imagination

options.text: To destroy a person's dreams or ambition by giving discouraging advice.
To make someone feel very interested in something
Advice someone to be more practical in an effort to tackle a problem.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **To make someone feel very interested in something.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **‘Fire the imagination’ means** to **make someone feel very enthusiastic **(inspired / interested) to do something.
 
• Example : *A successful athlete as a role model has the power to fire the imagination of the young children. *

 

Hence, the correct answer is '*To make someone feel very interested in something.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other idioms about 'enthusiasm':__**
 
• **(on the) edge of one's seat - ** Very interested in something and finds it both extremely exciting and nerve-wracking.
 
• **Ants in one’s pants -** People who have ants in their pants are very restless or excited about something
 
• **Go the extra mile ****- **If you** go the extra mile**, you do more than what is expected of you
 
• **Hold your horses -** If you tell someone to **hold their horses**, you think they are doing something too fast and should slow down and not rush into further action.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Parthian shot
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Parting hit'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom is **'Parting hit'. **
 
• **Parthian shot:** Parting hit is another term for 'Parting hit'. The meaning of it is: a remark that you make when you are leaving so that it has a stronger effect
 
 
• *Example: In a **Parthian shot,** the departing president is wrapping himself in a spurious mantle of civil liberty. *
 
 
 
• By reading the above explanation we find that the correct answer is **Option 1. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *Parting hit. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The story behind the idiom **'Parthian Shot' **as follows: 

 
 
• The Parthian shot is a light horse military tactic made famous by the Parthians, an ancient Iranian people.
 
• While being in real or feigned retreat, their horse archers would turn their bodies back in full gallop to shoot at the pursuing enemy.
 
• The maneuver required superb equestrian skills since the rider's hands were occupied by his composite bow.
 
• As the stirrup had not been invented at the time of the Parthians, the rider relied solely on pressure from his legs to guide his horse.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

The two brothers ___________ when their father died.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. 'fell out'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"fell out"** means to have a disagreement or argument and stop being friendly with someone. (झगड़ना)

 
 
• **Example: **They fell out over a trivial matter and didn’t speak for years.
 
 
 
• **"fell down"** refers to the act of losing balance and collapsing to the ground. (गिर जाना)
 
 
• **Example: **He fell down while running and scraped his knee.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct idiom to fill in the blank is **'fell out'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. 'fell out'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **fell down** (गिर जाना): The act of losing balance and collapsing to the ground.

 
 
• **Example:** He fell down while running and scraped his knee.
 
 
 
• **look down upon** (नजरअंदाज करना): To regard someone with a feeling of superiority.
 
 
• **Example: **She tends to look down upon people who don’t share her opinions.
 
 
 
• **got the sack** (नौकरी से निकाल दिया जाना): To be dismissed from one’s job.
 
 
• **Example:** He got the sack for consistently arriving late to work.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To lay someone by the heels
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option(1) i.e. To confine somebody in prison**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To lay someone by the heels"** means to imprison or confine someone. (किसी को जेल में डाल देना)

 
 
• **Example:** The notorious criminal was finally laid by the heels after a long pursuit.
 
 
 
• **"To confine somebody in prison"** refers to putting someone in jail or under restraint. (किसी को जेल में बंद करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The thief was laid by the heels after being caught red-handed.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of the idiom **'To lay someone by the heels'** is best expressed by **Option(1)**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option(1) i.e. To confine somebody in prison**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To gain support **(समर्थन प्राप्त करना): To receive backing or help from others.

 
 
• **Example:** He worked hard to gain support for his new project from the community.
 
 
 
• **To praise someone **(किसी की प्रशंसा करना): To express admiration or approval.
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher praised the student for his excellent performance in the exam.
 
 
 
• **To force someone for something** (किसी को कुछ करने के लिए मजबूर करना): To make someone do something against their will.
 
 
• **Example:** He was forced by his parents to pursue a career in medicine.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Tongue in cheek

options.text: In an ironic or insincere way.
Stop yourself from saying something hurtful.
Be gutsy and speak the unpleasant truth.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **In an ironic or insincere way**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• '**Tongue in cheek**' is an idiom that refers to something that is *not serious, not sincere, and is intended to highlight irony in a funny way*.
 
• This idiom can be used:
 
 
• As an Adjective__:
 __
 
• Example: Her latest film is a firmly **tongue-in-cheek** look at the world of advertising. 
 
• Here, 'tongue-in-cheek' is used as the way of how she looked; hence, it is an adjective__ here.
 
 
 
• As an Adverb: 
 __
 
• Example: Ramesh claimed then he was speaking **tongue-in-cheek.**
 
• Here, 'tongue-in-cheek' is a type of comment; hence, it is a noun__ here.
 
 
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 1**.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• This phrase is a literal reference to the facial expression created when putting the tongue in one's cheek. It also includes a wink to signify that what is being said is not to be taken seriously. The phrase first appeared in print in "The Fair maid of Perth" by Sir Walter Scott in 1928.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Pedal to the metal

options.text: Add more protection to an already strong shield.
Push a person to perform to its extreme.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **To drive very fast.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "pedal to the metal" is often used to describe driving a vehicle at full throttle or with maximum speed.
 
• It implies pushing the accelerator pedal all the way to the floor ("metal" referring to the floorboard of a car).

Thus, the correct answer is **option 3**.

Example: We are going to have to put the** pedal to the metal **if we want to finish on time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Build something big by yourself:**

 
 
• This option does not express the meaning of the idiom "pedal to the metal." The idiom is related to driving or speed and does not refer to building or creating something.
 
 
 
• **Add more protection to an already strong shield:**
 
 
• This option does not express the meaning of the idiom "pedal to the metal." The idiom is about driving fast and does not involve adding protection to a shield or any form of defensive action.
 
 
 
• **Push a person to perform to its extreme:**
 
 
• This option is somewhat related to the idiom "pedal to the metal." It captures the essence of pushing someone to perform at their maximum or pushing them to their limits. However, it does not specifically convey the notion of speed or driving, which is the primary meaning of the idiom.
